ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath: The North Star only points the way; it is never the destination. Find your own path, Traveler.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Aurena: And so, one unsolved question was hidden behind that confident smile.
Leaving behind the glory that sleeps somewhere beyond the gold, and this moment that somehow feels so trifling.
…What shape the proof at the end of the light will take, and what she herself will become, none can say yet,
yet Aurena will not cease her analysis, the silver brooch clutched in her hand.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Bismut: And so, the way to write a story was forgotten amid refusal.
Leaving the picture of who they are still a blank page.
…Yet the next sentence upon the page's white expanse, which no one can foretell,
will be drawn by a brush that is wholly Bismuth's own.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Cetus_: And so, the promise to meet again came to its end.
An ending no one wished for, leaving behind the feelings that remained.
…yet upon a path borrowed from no one's hand, the footsteps
will become, for the first time, truly Cetus's own to walk.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Husk_0: And so, one passing rumor faded away.
Feeling neither the aching emotion, nor the wind that brushed on by.
…Yet the hand still reaches out into the empty air, and whatever it is he seeks to feel,
Shell will not yet withdraw that hand.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Lacert: And so, the voice that warned of a second tragedy was buried beneath the gunfire.
Leaving behind a longed-for name, and a quiet answer lingering in the empty air.
…How he will meet that reprieved moment, none can say, but the music etched within him,
Lacerta will chase still, his finger resting on the trigger.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Mist_0: And so, the conversation that made her look inward scattered like mist.
Leaving behind words swallowed in bitterness, and a voice still out of reach.
…Whether that mist will lift or grow thicker, none can say, but the voice within it,
Mist will walk toward it—not to protect, but to face it at last.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Nachia: And so, the offer that bore the name of salvation faded away.
Leaving behind one name that still remains, and a forgotten forest.
…Whether the leaves will sprout again, none can say, but with steps she has chosen herself,
Nachia will press onward without stopping.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Vesper: And so, the blazing flame and enmity were left as but a handful of ash.
Upon a body ever fading, leaving behind only a burning faith without substance.
…What he will set aflame, none can say, but with his fire that transcends right and wrong,
Vesper will serve, without doubt, only his own sun.
ui.Ending_Narrator_StarlessPath_Hero_Yubar_: And so, the starlight of two gods, meant to be shared, faded away alone.
Leaving behind subtly unsettled feelings, and a true sky still out of reach.
…Whether he can touch the sky, or whether even that sky is but the floor of somewhere else, none can say,
yet Yubar will gather up his own starlight still.
ui.Ending_Polaris_AbsorbedByMoraMare: It's not over yet. It can't be over. And I'm so... so hungry...

ui.Guide_AttackDamageAbilityPower_0: A Traveler's basic attack deals damage equal to their [Attack Damage], while most Memories deal damage based on [Ability Power]. You can check which stat a Memory or Essence scales with by the icons (<sprite=2><sprite=1>) in the tooltip description.
ui.Guide_AttackEffect_0: Some Essences have an [attack effect] that triggers each time the Traveler performs a basic attack. This effect generally doesn't trigger on Memory damage.
ui.Guide_Cold_0: Memories that deal Cold damage apply [Cold] to enemies. Cold slows enemies down.
ui.Guide_CritChance_0: According to this probability, the Traveler's [basic attack] becomes a [Critical Strike], dealing double damage. Damage from Memories is not affected by Critical Strike Chance.
ui.Guide_Dark_0: Memories that deal Dark damage apply [Dark] stacks to enemies. Enemies corrupted by darkness take `DewElementals::DarkDamageAmpPerStack|percent*100` increased damage from Dark damage per stack, and can be stacked up to 5 times.
ui.Guide_EditMode_0:
You can freely change your Memories and Essences at any time through [Edit mode]. To enter Edit mode, press `editSkillHold,editSkillToggle`.

In Edit mode, you can also check the Traveler's stats on the bottom left of the screen.
ui.Guide_Essence_0: [Essences] are mysterious gems you can equip to Memories to give them special effects. These effects are treated as part of that Memory. When you equip multiple Essences to the same Memory, they can interact to create chain effects.
ui.Guide_Fire_0: Memories that deal Fire damage apply stacks of [Fire] to enemies. Fire stacks inflict [Burn] damage over time, scaling with the number of stacks and the enemy's level, and can stack without limit. [Burn] damage doesn't trigger Essences.
ui.Guide_Hunt_0:
The Master of Dreams doesn't welcome outsiders. The monsters he created, known as the [Hunters], will pursue you relentlessly.
These [Hunters] take over adjacent rooms with each movement turn, except the room with the exit. Entering a room occupied by the Hunters is extremely dangerous. [Move quickly!]
ui.Guide_ItemSharing_0: To let others pick up Memories and Essences that have dropped for you, [Share] them by pinging (`ping`) the item. Unequipped Memories and Essences are shared automatically and can be picked up by others.
ui.Guide_Light_0: Memories that deal Light damage apply [Light] stacks to enemies. Enemies exposed to light take `DewElementals::LightDamageAmpPerStack|percent*100` increased damage from Light damage per stack, and can be stacked up to 5 times.
ui.Guide_MeleeBasicAttack_0: The basic attack of a [Melee Traveler] deals area damage, dealing 100% of their Attack Damage to the main target and 50% damage to other targets.
ui.Guide_Merchant_0: You can purchase Memories and Essences from the [Merchant] using Gold, or sell your own Memories and Essences to them.
ui.Guide_MirageSkin_0: Deep in The Rapids, some monsters appear with [Mirage Skin]. Mirage Skin makes them Unstoppable and immune to crowd control effects such as stun and root, while granting special abilities that make them extremely dangerous. Delusion - Reduces healing received by Travelers. Oblivion - Prevents Travelers from casting Memories for a short time. Oppression - Stuns Travelers. Pulverization - Destroys Travelers' shields. Sanctification - Makes nearby monsters immune to damage. The deeper you venture into The Rapids, the more varied and deadly types of Mirage Skin you'll encounter.
ui.Guide_OverCrits_0:
If [Critical Strike Chance] exceeds 100%, the Traveler's basic attacks will always be Critical Strikes and also have a chance to deal even greater additional damage.
For example, with 120% Critical Strike Chance, there is a 20% chance to deal triple damage and an 80% chance to deal double damage. With 220% Critical Strike Chance, there is a 20% chance to deal quadruple damage and an 80% chance to deal triple damage.
ui.Guide_PingsAndEmotes_0:
You can use [Ping](`ping`) on monsters, Memories, Essences, and more to alert your teammates.
Press and hold the [Emote] button(`emote`) to open the emote wheel, then hover over the desired emote and release to express your current mood.

On gamepad, tap the assigned button to ping or hold it to use emotes.
ui.Guide_Potions_0:
When you defeat enemies, there is a 2.5% chance they will drop a Health Potion. When collected, all nearby Travelers recover a small amount of Health.

The chance of a Health Potion dropping increases as the Traveler's Health decreases, up to a maximum of 5%. Heroic Bosses and Mini Bosses have a 100% chance to drop a Health Potion.
ui.Guide_Rift_0:
You can use [rifts] to move from your current location to adjacent rooms. Your expedition must defeat enemies and reach each dream's exit to move on to the next one.

Interact with a rift or press `worldMap` to open the Dream Map.
ui.Guide_SkillHaste_0: [Memory Haste] reduces the cooldown of all Memories. For example, if you have 100 Memory Haste, the cooldown will be reduced 100% faster. For Ultimate abilities, it increases the charge speed at the same rate.
ui.Guide_Skill_0: [Memories] are magical recollections that can be used during combat in The Rapids. You can equip, unequip, or swap Memories at any time while in The Rapids.
ui.Guide_Ultimates_0:
[Ultimate Memories] do not have a standard cooldown and can only be used when their charge reaches 100%. The Ultimate charges whenever the Traveler deals or receives damage, and this rate is affected by Memory Haste.
Cooldown reduction effects applied to Ultimates are converted at a rate of 1 second to 1%.
ui.Guide_UniqueMemoriesAndEssences_0: By defeating [Heroic Bosses] and claiming their souls, you can sometimes obtain Memories or Essences that cannot be acquired by any other means.
ui.Guide_Well_0: At the [Well], you can use Dream Dust to empower Memories or Essences. Empowering raises the level of Memories and improves the quality of Essences, making them more powerful.
ui.Hero_Aurena_Description: Aurena is a sage from the Lunar Arcanum Society who was expelled for researching forbidden knowledge. She is a battle healer who dismantles her own life force to wield its power.
ui.Hero_Aurena_Story:
Aurena is a brilliant scholar who studies the mysterious powers of dreams. She discovers and learns to harness the dream power known as "Dismantling Force," but this process involves numerous forbidden experiments.
Though ultimately expelled from the Society, Aurena willingly enters The Rapids to fully unravel the world of dreams.
Aurena believes bringing back perfect knowledge will restore her honor, unaware of the true price she may have to pay.
ui.Hero_Aurena_Subtitle: Expelled Sage of the Lunar Arcanum Society
ui.Hero_Bismuth_Description: Bismuth is the fusion of an empty, nameless spellbook and an ordinary blind girl. She moves swiftly and deals sustained ranged damage.
ui.Hero_Bismuth_Story: When two consciousnesses became one, both the book and the girl disappeared, and Bismuth was born. The girl had always longed to see the world, while the book wished to become the protagonist of its own story. As they entered The Rapids to fulfill each other's wishes, their minds became intertwined, yet their vision has never been clearer. So together, as a new being named Bismuth, they entered The Rapids to write their story.
ui.Hero_Cetus_Description: Cetus is a ranged fighter who unleashes the powerful frost imbued within his body. He locks down enemies with freezing cold and grants shields to protect himself and his allies.
ui.Hero_Cetus_Story:
Cetus was once the most ruthless and loyal executioner of the Lucid Sect, but he chose the path of an apostate after uncovering the ugly truth: the sect was using the power of dreams to deceive the world.
Cruel experiments conducted during his imprisonment imbued his body with an inescapable, biting frost. Having broken out of his cell, Cetus now steps into the heart of The Rapids to fulfill his purpose and face his sins head-on.
ui.Hero_Cetus_Subtitle: Frost Executioner Bearing the Chains of Atonement
ui.Hero_Husk_Description: Shell is the perfect instrument of slaughter, incapable of feeling emotion or pain. An assassin who exploits enemy weaknesses with unpredictable movements, eliminating targets in the most efficient way possible.
ui.Hero_Husk_Story: The soul of a once-infamous assassin now resides in a wooden puppet that feels neither emotion nor pain. To him, targets were merely obstacles to be removed, and his blade would find the most efficient path without hesitation. Despite being a perfect tool of slaughter, he is plagued by an unfillable void. He comes to realize that his lost emotions are connected to the world of dreams. In search of his true body and hoping to quench his endless thirst, Shell enters The Rapids, the origin of everything.
ui.Hero_Husk_Subtitle: Manufactured Assassin, Wooden Doll with a Soul
ui.Hero_Lacerta_Description: Lacerta is a former Royal Guard sniper and hunter skilled with firearms and gunpowder. He is used to taking out enemies from a distance.
ui.Hero_Lacerta_Story:
After leaving the Royal Guard, Lacerta settled into life as an ordinary hunter. Several years ago, his wife vanished before his eyes, consumed by blue flames.
Recently, Lacerta uncovered clues linking her disappearance to dreams and the Lucid Sect. He enters The Rapids, determined to find out what happened to his wife.
ui.Hero_Mist_Description: Mist is a brave duelist of noble birth. Her agile fighting style allows her to dodge deadly attacks and quickly take down her enemies.
ui.Hero_Mist_Story:
Mist's younger sister, Astrid, has recently vanished, leaving behind only a letter. In it, Astrid claims she has joined the Lucid Sect, a secret group devoted to dreams.
But Mist is convinced her sister would never make such a choice willingly—she must have been taken. Determined to rescue Astrid, Mist enters The Rapids.
ui.Hero_Nachia_Description: Nachia is a spirit mage of the dream world and guardian of the Ethereal Forest. She can summon spirits that follow her and fight by her side, dealing steady damage.
ui.Hero_Nachia_Story:
The once peaceful Ethereal Forest was transformed into the "Forest of Turbulence" for reasons unknown, forcing its guardian, Nachia, to leave her home. Awakening in an unfamiliar place, Nachia discovered her Memories in pieces. She does not know why she is here or what happened to change the forest.
All that remains are faint connections with spirits, fragmented memories, and a sadness she cannot explain. Nachia now wanders The Rapids, searching for answers about her past and the tragedy that befell her forest.
ui.Hero_Nachia_Subtitle: Spirit Mage of the Dream World, Guardian of the Ethereal Forest
ui.Hero_Vesper_Description: Vesper is the leader of the Order of the Sacred Flame and a ruthless inquisitor. He fights at close range, holding back enemies while dealing heavy damage.
ui.Hero_Vesper_Story:
Vesper, leader of the Order of the Sacred Flame and a devout follower of the sun god El'pyros, seeks to purge all heretics who oppose El'pyros's will.
While raiding an outpost of the Lucid Sect, a group of dream worshippers, Vesper and his subordinates discover a dimensional rift leading to The Rapids.
Seizing the opportunity, he enters The Rapids with his followers, intent on striking down the false god they serve.
But now, his subordinates are nowhere to be found.
ui.Hero_Vesper_Subtitle: Ruthless Inquisitor of the Order of the Sacred Flame
ui.Hero_Yubar_Description: Yubar is a fantastical being born from dreams, a deity who governs the creation and destruction of stars. He uses powerful magic to deal heavy damage from a distance.
ui.Hero_Yubar_Story:
Yubar suddenly awakens somewhere in The Rapids. The immense power he once possessed is gone, and when he reaches out, the stars no longer gather at his command.
Something feels off... and oddly intriguing. Determined to find out why, he sets out to find answers within The Rapids.
ui.Hero_Yubar_Subtitle: Born of Dreams, God of Stars

ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_0: It's okay. This is just a dream.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_1: I guess it's not my fault.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_3: You'll do better next time, right?
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_4: If only I had dodged that.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_5: Nevertheless, you failed to wake up.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_6: The soil in The Rapids has grown more fertile.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_7: The Rapids remain at peace today.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Dark_0: In the end, darkness consumed you.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Dark_1: It's so dark, not even a body could be found.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Dark_2: There's nothing left behind those dark eyes.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Fire_1: Whas this your idea of getting a tan?
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Aur: Taking risks always comes with a price.
Your health comes first. Don't push yourself too hard.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Bis: We always wanted to see the world, but not like this.
The mystical colors slowly faded away from them.
In a place both foreign and familiar, they concluded their story.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Cet: Forgive me... In the end, once again, I protected nothing.
Sadly, the chains were never loosed, and the helm was never lifted.
Only after he closed his eyes was he freed from his guilt.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Hus: A servant without purpose has no reason to exist.
It is truly pitiful to not know what to feel even at death's door.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Lac: Maybe this was just too much for a reptile.
Oh no. I never like seeing animals die.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Mis: The saber was found nearby, bent like a noodle.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Nac: Who will feed the dogs now?
As time passed, an undying spring blossomed beneath her staff.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Ves: Maybe their faith just wasn't enough.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Hero_Yub: Even the god of stars wasn't much, after all.
He once created the stars, but he couldn't save himself.
Perhaps it's okay, since he was never alive to begin with.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Ice_0: You were discovered by a later party, frozen for eternity.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Ice_2: The ground is cold as ice.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Light_0: That's one brilliant way to go.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Light_1: You were shining so bright, I almost didn't realize you were dead.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Light_2: Staring at a bright light too long can make you go blind.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_MoraToEv: Ah, at last! How long I have waited for this dish to be complete...
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_MoraToTr: In the end, you too became one glittering proof. Congratulations—this must be the very constant you searched so long for.
You vowed to erase the protagonist from your story—yet in the end, it was I who wrote this ending. A fitting conclusion, wouldn't you agree?
In the end, you failed to protect anyone. Again. So wonderfully consistent, aren't you.
Well? Do you feel something at last? That sensation you sought so desperately—and it had to be this very moment.
A third tragedy—oh, what a rerun this is! Do try to remember it this time, won't you? Don't just erase it again.
A hair too late, once again. The mist may lift, yet you remain right where you always were.
Still hesitating, I see. That tenderness is precisely what brought you here. Truly, a sight I never tire of, no matter how many times I watch it.
Look at that. You claimed faith alone would sustain you. And yet, without substance, you fade so beautifully. Isn't it lovely?
See? In the end you were only a single line in someone else's tale. And this ending—rather a lovely sentence, don't you think?
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Spider_0: Looks like the local spiders just got their meal for the day.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Spider_1: Less than an hour later, not even your bones remained.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_GameOver_Spider_2: Pretty sure bug spray won't cut it with a spider that size.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_PureWhiteDream: At last, you have achieved what you desired.
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_PureWhiteDream_He: I was right all along! Now even the Society won't be able to refute my claims.
Now let's make the world our story. The story of Bismuth!
…Primus has heeded my words at last. Only now can everything be set right.
...I can feel it. Truly... it's been so long since I felt warmth.
Finally... I see you again. Iris. Have you... waited long?
Astrid, I can hear your voice... I was so worried.
Little Belpho, it's been a while. I've missed you. Truly...
The purification of this world does not end here.
Huzzah! Is this the true power of the divine? It suits this form most splendidly!
ui.InGame_Result_Subtitle_StarlessPath: Now, before you, lies only nameless darkness and your own footprints.

ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_00: Long long ago, there lived a man named Primus.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_02: Within the depths of dreams, Primus became the very first god.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_03: But thereafter, the barrier between dreams and reality shattered.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_04: and terrible monsters began pouring forth from the realm between,
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_06: Some saw this as a catastrophe. While others saw it as an opportunity.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_07: They say that those who reach the deepest depths of dreams,
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_08: can achieve anything their heart desires.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_09: And so, countless beings entered The Rapids,
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_10: each grasping their own reasons, and their own purposes.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_11: But these, these are their dreams.
ui.IntroVideo_Subtitle_13: What is your shape of dreams?

ui.LucidDream_FishScales_Description:
The amount of shield you can maintain at once is capped at 100% of your maximum health, and monster attacks deal damage to the Traveler's maximum health.

You can mitigate some of this max health damage by activating a Shrine of Guidance, and the damage is reset each time you enter a new world.

ui.LucidDream_HarmlessWhispers_Description: Most Heroic Bosses can now be affected by crowd control effects, but their maximum health and damage are slightly increased.
ui.LucidDream_KindArmadillo_Description: All Mirage Skins are replaced with Armor Mirage Skins, which grant no special effects.
ui.LucidDream_MadLife_Description: All monsters try harder to predict Travelers' movements. (They may not always succeed.)

ui.LucidDream_Overpopulation_Description: Increases the number of monsters by 50%, excluding bosses.
ui.LucidDream_PrudentJellyfish_Description:
Most cooldown reduction effects are weakened.

When reducing cooldowns with Memory Haste and Memory upgrades, cooldowns now converge to 50% of their base value instead of 0 seconds. Effects that reduce the current cooldown by a flat amount of time, rather than a percentage, are also 50% weaker.
ui.LucidDream_SparklingDreamFlask_Descripti: Health Potions and Shrine of Guidance now grant Dream Dust instead of healing.
ui.LucidDream_TheDarkestUrge_Description: All characters are unable to distinguish between friend and foe, and monsters devour each other to grow stronger.

ui.Nametag_April_EverlastingAutumn_Descript: A spring scent that lasts forever.
ui.Nametag_Boss_CleverGirl_Description: From the shattered sea of gluttony, a nameless shard emerged. The wounded god saw his own scars in that fragment and forged his regrets into a blade. It's edge, shaped by guilt and tempered by his cruelty, became the most loyal sword. This blade reflects not the uncertain eyes of its master, but only the face of a perfect tyrant.
ui.Nametag_Boss_CorruptedForestKeeper_Descr: His touch was the whisper of azure leaves, a guidepost for the lost. Yet at the tips of broken branches, he bloomed thorns from crimson dreams. Now his forest becomes a trap, its end nothing but hungry brambles.
ui.Nametag_Boss_EmptyFaithBurningHeart_Desc: He was a gentle mountain, embracing his dearest friend, yet beneath his shadow, he harbored the fiery heat of a heart that could melt all things. He turned his own body into an altar and imprisoned himself, raising an illusion from his purest memories. Now, he offers a cup with a smile, and when the cup is empty, he stains the altar with his friend's blood.
ui.Nametag_Boss_FirstChallenger_Description:
He was the first blade to point its edge at the God of Dreams, his blade was the ridge of snow-capped mountains, and his edge was the song of giants.
Yet how could one cleave the anvil that forged the world? The sword shattered into pieces, and his kingdom turned to dust from the shock of its own breaking sound.
Now he is a rusted blade drifting over his own fragments. The first defeat that proves the god's power, and the first courage that proves one can challenge him.
ui.Nametag_Boss_Gluttony_Description:
He was a wise gardener who tended the sky garden, and the blue, cloud-soaked flowers were his only friends.
One day, when sorrowful rain fell and poison seeped into his roots, the gardener became a pest that coveted the flowers.
From the depths of shattered petals, he turned into a swarm of locusts. Even if another hand snapped off parts of him, that vast hunger would only drift on to the next flower bed.
ui.Nametag_Boss_HarmonyDiscord_Description:
His brush is a single, bold stroke soaked with the ink of hope. His movements are the steadfast will that writes new beginnings upon a blank canvas, where every blurred trace is turned into proper letters under the first stroke of the white night.
She is a solid stone, grinding lingering regrets into essence. Her cooling presence brings the scent of ink that calms a restless mind. Every obsession is worn away on the inkstone of a cold moon.
All souls are shaped and written here, each one opening a new chapter. Any creature that disturbs the white rice paper is simply a misplaced drop of ink.
ui.Nametag_Boss_LoveEmbroideredNightSky_Des:
The universe drew her as the brightest star, yet she refused her destined orbit and wished to become a comet forging her own path.
So she cast herself into the black void, breaking her orbit, believing that stealing light from other stars was freedom.
Yet the wandering star knows not that her path is merely spinning, drawn by another gravity.
Nor that the veil of broken starlight still guards her night.
ui.Nametag_Boss_LoveEmbroideredNightSky_Nam: Love Embroidered in the Night Sky
ui.Nametag_Boss_MawOfDoom_Description:
Where the nightmare seeped through the world and passed on, a single uncollected scrap opened its eyes, leaving behind nothing but an empty belly.
Devouring every warmth it met without discrimination, it grew, and one day it flung its maw open without hesitation even before the very thing that birthed it.
Yet all that suffering gave in return was mocking laughter, and the hunger, unable to recognize even its own origin, remains unsated still.
ui.Nametag_Boss_Polaris_Description:
She was but a lone echo left behind by longing, yet she refused to dwell within that resonance and became a star that burns of its own accord.
To shield the frail flames flickering toward darkness, she took a stranger's wick as her own, and consuming herself, she lights the way for the weak.
But she failed to see the soot seeping into that flame, and what awaits at the journey's end—even she does not know.
ui.Nametag_Boss_Polaris_Name: The Star That Chose Its Own Light
ui.Nametag_Boss_Radiance_Description:
In the days when all spirits knelt beneath his banner and all elements sang of his deeds, the light of his radiant throne knew no dimming.
Yet those radiant days lost their light, and the brand of rebellion was carved upon him. In the ruins of a nameless dimension, he became a ghost that none remember.
Breaking the silence of those ruins, a whisper blooms. The king without a throne gathers his army once more beneath a forgotten banner.
ui.Nametag_Boss_SeekerOfEndlessPower_Descri:
Having drunk from every fountain of knowledge, yet with his thirst unquenched, the sage finally reached the bottom of the well in the abyss.
The pilgrim became a plunderer, learning to steal water from other vessels to moisten his fractured soul.
Drought has dried up all his rivers, and he remains alone, licking the bitter dregs at the bottom of his own vessel.
ui.Nametag_Boss_StarIlluminatingTheQueen_De:
For her, he painted an eternal masterpiece: the night sky. But she, coveting his creation, trapped the artist within his own canvas.
Now the sole admirer, the queen shines alone upon the jet-black paint, drunk on the arrogance that it was all for her.
Yet from behind the canvas, whenever a strange color threatens to stain it, the painter quietly wipes away the blemish with an unseen brushstroke.
ui.Nametag_Boss_StarIlluminatingTheQueen_Na: The Star That Illuminates the Queen
ui.Nametag_Boss_TheFirstDreamer_Description:
The Dream Guardian sings, letting a longed-for voice resound in a room full of silence.
The Dream Tyrant commands, demanding that all the world's noise be quieted for that song.
A human understands that an echo with no reply is only an empty sound.
ui.Nametag_General_EndOfBeginning_Descripti:
Do you remember how the empty canvas was once a dazzling white? It was a perfect silence, a world where nothing existed.
You simply wanted to place a single, tiny dot on that pure world. Something like a familiar face or a faint warmth.
The moment you yearned for a color other than white, atop the tower of shells, you realized the very first dot was actually a smudge.
ui.Nametag_General_PrincessDream_Descriptio:
The princess's palace gleams with a thousand chandeliers shining day and night, a dazzling prison where not even a sliver of shadow is allowed.
So the princess dreams of a single beam of sunlight slipping through old, creaking window frames, casting its glow on a dusty floor.
Those who stand in the brightest place can never hide in darkness. Only when she closes her eyes does she wander, searching for a humble corner somewhere.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Aurena0_Description: A child born from forgotten ink and a final breath. Solving his incomplete equation was her only purpose.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Aurena1_Description: They called her boldness heresy, yet the exiled sage finally found the answer: the alchemy of knowledge that turns the lead of ignorance into pure gold.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Aurena2_Description: She carries yesterday's moon in her heart, holding unfinished gold as she moves forward. She does not realize she herself is scattering into noble dust, the final ingredient for the ultimate transmutation.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Bismuth0_Description:
One was a crystal lantern, cold for it could not hold light,
The other was a lonely flame, burning alone in darkness with no vessel to contain it.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Bismuth1_Description:
The flame willingly seeped into the lantern, and the lantern embraced light for the very first time.
The story gained its first sentence, the girl gained her first world—what a perfect exchange.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Bismuth2_Description:
The flame sees the world only through the lantern's hue, and the lantern exists only through the light trapped within.
United as one, they wander still through the eternal night, illuminating each other.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Cetus0_Description:
He was a whale cleaving the deep, yet his body was a blade bound in the chains of a god.
He passed judgment on those who sank, believing it the only current that led toward the light.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Cetus1_Description:
Yet within the darkness he cleaved lay another abyss, one that laid false claim to the light.
The blade shattered into ice, and the chains bit into flesh, carving a winter that would never thaw.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Cetus2_Description:
Now, clad in a broken helm, he swims alone, bearing ice that will not melt upon his back.
Yearning for a current that is no one's but his own, until he reaches the gate of the silent god.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Husk0_Description: His soul was a precarious flame, twisted together with sin and warmth. He prayed for this painful light to be extinguished.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Husk1_Description: As he wished, the flame dimmed, leaving only a handful of cold ashes in his chest. Instead of peace, he found only bitter cold and the complete darkness known to those who have lost their light.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Husk2_Description: The ashes wear a smiling mask, sinking into the abyss of dreams in search of lost embers. The wood that has turned to ash forgets it can never burn again.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Lacerta0_Description: His feet always followed the only path he knew: a march of loyalty to his king and faith in his comrades. It was a perfect march without a single misstep.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Lacerta1_Description: But the map given to him by a nameless stranger showed a path to a unique cabin in an unknown forest, the only one of its kind in the world. For the first time in his life, he stopped his march and chose that path.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Lacerta2_Description: The map has turned to ashes, leaving him alone on the road. Guided by the afterimage of blue flames, he walks again along the path where his tears have dried, as if it were his very first journey.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Mist0_Description: The teal vine torn from the fortress wall learned to survive by rooting in nameless crevices, feeding on smiles instead of sunlight and drinking the dew of tempered blades instead of rain.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Mist1_Description: Now, in a land where those smiles never return and even the stone crevices feel empty, the vine no longer hides.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Mist2_Description: Covering itself with thorns, the vine crawls into the abyss of dreams to ensnare the world that uprooted it. All this to reclaim the one warmth that once touched its roots.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Nachia0_Description:
One was the forest's beating heart, and one was the wild lungs that carried its breath.
Their rhythm and breathing wove together, flowing the world's most peaceful song.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Nachia1_Description:
One day when breath turned poisonous, every song became a cough and every air became venom.
Now the heart beats desperately alone, sealing shut its final vessels.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Nachia2_Description:
When at last it broke through its own ribs and stepped outside, the heart had forgotten everything.
Carrying only the inexplicable pain felt from where the empty lungs once were.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Vesper0_Description: His soul was cold iron forged in a smithy devoid of light. He learned to call the hammer blows upon his body a blessing.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Vesper1_Description: At last he came to worship the great furnace, the sun, leading other soft irons before it. He promised not warmth, but the perfect form that can only be gained after melting away.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Vesper2_Description: So when another furnace opened its burning mouth to the world, he did not hesitate. To a true believer, questioning the source of the flames is little more than a meaningless luxury.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Yubar0_Description: His kingdom was perfect, yet it was only a landscape trapped within a mirror. He was simply the most brilliant reflection in it.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Yubar1_Description: Until one day, a crack appeared in the mirror, and he discovered eyes watching him from the other side.
ui.Nametag_Heroes_Yubar2_Description: So rather than remain an eternal illusion, he shattered the mirror of creation with his own hands and walked upon its fragments. No longer reflected, he became the true hand, the one who gazes into the mirror.

ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToAurena_0: None are so blind as those who believe themselves wise.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToAurena_1: Do you truly think you've discovered the truth, arrogant one?
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToAurena_2: Leave this place. Your tragedy is inevitable.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToBismuth_0: I'm sorry, but you are not the protagonist.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToBismuth_1: You've lost yourself, yet you seek dreams? How preposterous.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToBismuth_2: You don't understand that reality is not a fairy tale world.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToCetus_0: You believed in false doctrine. I have never demanded faith, nor do I care for it.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToCetus_1: No words are needed. The dream is my reality, and I shall seal it away for eternity.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToCetus_2: Turn back now, or be frozen for all eternity.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToHusk_0: How pitiful. Do you truly still believe yourself to be human?
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToHusk_1: A puppet of slaughter yearning for wishes? That's too much for the likes of you.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToHusk_2: A soulless puppet wishing for sensation - at least you won't feel disappointment.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToLacerta_0: Lacerta, I warned you to never to return here...
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToLacerta_2: There are no second chances, Lacerta.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToMist_0: Your story is tragic, but who lives without suffering?
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToMist_1: You and your sibling remain uninvited guests in my domain.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToMist_2: How foolish. Can you not tell courage from recklessness?
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToNachia_0: I sense a distant, eerie energy from your tragedy. How unpleasant.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToNachia_1: Guardian of a fading forest, why do you hasten your own demise?
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToNachia_2: You who couldn't protect your own dreams, why interfere with others' reality? Begone.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToVesper_0: Consumed by emotion, you stumble toward an inevitable mistake...
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToVesper_1: Your justice belongs to an empty god. I hope the sacrifice proves worthy.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToVesper_2: Zealot, this reality is one your own foolishness created.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToYubar_0: Such arrogant ambitions you harbor, false deity.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToYubar_1: Master of a dreamless realm—how utterly pitiful.
ui.RoomMod_Hunted_PrimusWarnToYubar_2: Your fate would find you even in stillness, yet you race toward oblivion.

[Move Direction:] Dodge and some dash Memories will be cast in the move direction.

ui.Settings_GameplayPlatform_disableSoftwar: Uses the operating system cursor instead of the in-game cursor. Cursor size and color adjustments will not be not available.
ui.Settings_GameplayPlatform_enableCrossPla: Play alongside players on other platforms during co-op. Turn this off to see only lobbies from your own platform in the lobby list, and you'll only be able to play with players on the same platform.
ui.Settings_GameplayPlatform_enableDevelope: Enables the developer console for mod development and debugging.
ui.Settings_GameplayPlatform_skipIntro_Desc: Skips the intro that plays when the game starts.
ui.Settings_GameplayPlatform_skipPhotosensi: Skips the Photosensitivity Warning shown when the game starts.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_abbreviateBigDamag: Shows damage and healing in shortened format for easier reading.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_confirmMemoryEditB:
Requires you to hold the button to prevent accidentally selling or upgrading items.

ui.Settings_GameplayUser_cursorColor_Descri: Changes the color of the mouse cursor.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_cursorScale_Descri: Adjusts the size of the mouse cursor.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_enableArachnophobi: Spiders are displayed as lizardmen. Text mentioning 'spiders' (names, descriptions, etc.) remains unchanged, and this only applies to your own screen.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_enableProfanityFil: Filters out profanity and inappropriate expressions in player names, chat messages, etc.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_gamepadVibrationSt: Adjust the strength of the controller vibration.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_highlightCharacter: Highlights characters such as Travelers, monsters, etc. when you hover your mouse cursor over them.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_killScreenEffectsS: Adjust the brightness effect when killing enemies.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_reduceOtherPlayerE: Lowers the intensity of visual effects (particles, lighting, flashes, etc.) from Memories used by other players.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_resetTutorial_Desc: Resets tutorial progress and replay all game instructions.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_screenShakeStrengt: Adjusts the strength of screen shaking in the game.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_shareItemsWhenDrop: In co-op, dropping Memories or Essence will automatically share them with allies. If disabled, you must ping the item after dropping it to share it.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_showHunterWarning_: Once per game, displays a confirmation message before traveling to a location occupied by a Hunter.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_uiScale_Descriptio: Adjusts the size of UI elements including menus and in-game HUD.
ui.Settings_GameplayUser_unlockSkillsOutsid: Move Memories and Essences anytime without switching to Edit Mode.
ui.Settings_Graphics_activityAdaptivePerfor: Monitors the game's framerate (FPS) in real-time and automatically disables minor visual effects during performance drops to maintain a smooth gameplay experience.
ui.Settings_Graphics_enableDynamicResolutio: When GPU load is high, the rendering resolution is lowered in real time to maintain the target frame rate, then restored to the original resolution once there's headroom. The screen may appear slightly blurry.
ui.Settings_Graphics_fogQuality_Description: Adjusts the quality of fog. May increase GPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_particleEffectQuality_: Adjusts the quality of particle effects. May increase CPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_playerAbilityCount_Des: Adjusts the number of player memories, essence effects, and projectiles that can be displayed on screen simultaneously. Lower settings prioritize performance by not displaying some abilities on screen or simplifying calculations.
ui.Settings_Graphics_screenSpaceReflections: Creates realistic reflections on smooth surfaces in real-time. May increase GPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_shaderQuality_Descript: Adjusts the quality of other shader effects. May increase GPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_shadowQuality_Descript: Adjusts shadow detail. May increase GPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_terrainQuality_Descrip: Adjusts the quality of terrain. May increase GPU usage.
ui.Settings_Graphics_textureQuality_Descrip: Adjusts the quality of detailed texture rendering for terrain, objects, and characters. Usually has minimal impact on GPU usage, but has a greater effect on VRAM consumption.
ui.Settings_Graphics_vSync_Description: Syncs game frames to your monitor's refresh rate to eliminate screen tearing. Disables frame limits when active.
ui.Settings_Graphics_vegetationQuality_Desc: Adjusts the density of grass and foliage. May increase GPU usage.

ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main1_Content_0: {IMAGE} "…and with that, I conclude." Aurena let out a sigh. To present a written work for tens of minutes was wearying, no matter how worn-out the subject. But the real test began now. She straightened her posture at the podium. It was time to field the question-and-answer session that followed. The final gateway to recognition as a sage of the Arcanum was the most vexing and perilous, yet at the same time the most valuable. The sages invited to serve as review panelists leafed silently through the printed materials before them. Some had taken notes while listening to Aurena's presentation on the spot; others had long since dog-eared pages here and there, or marked passages with colorful bookmarks. Tilting her head absentmindedly, Aurena grew conscious of the large, vigorous golden ornament that rose on either side of her head—reminiscent of an artiodactyl's antlers—and tensed the nape of her neck. At the faint jingling, the less-than-friendly gazes of a few panelists lingered briefly above her head before returning to the printouts. Aurena, however, paid it no mind. Surely the esteemed sages of the Arcanum would not render their decision on the basis of a candidate's attire rather than her erudition and accomplishments? "Quite a bold subject to choose for a work composed at Half Moon standing, isn't it?" "I am fully aware of that." she answered the first sage to speak. "Half Moon" was, of course, a convenient designation used only within the Arcanum Society. Those granted the right to study at the Society were Crescents; those who had attained a certain scholarly accomplishment were Half Moons; and those who, by the recognition of the Society's members, became one of the sages of the Arcanum were, naturally, Full Moons. This was not an actual astronomical phenomenon but a classification by shape alone. For were one to take it strictly, the only path remaining to a Full Moon sage of the Arcanum would be to wane through the third quarter and the old crescent until, at last, becoming the dark new moon and vanishing without a trace—which would turn the title into a curse. In any case, a silence followed that opening remark for a while. Why is no one asking anything? Aurena shifted her gaze irritably. The sages had the crowns of their heads all but fully exposed, noses buried in the written work. Watching them, the suspicion she had barely suppressed—lest it impede her posture of seeking truth—threatened to raise its head once more. Do these old fogeys even truly understand my subject? she thought. The theme of discovering a new force that expands the very table of the existing natural laws would surely be daunting—not only from the position generating the discourse, Aurena herself, but also from the position attempting to critique it. It made no difference that the people seated as panelists, however cloistered within the Seven Spires of Truth, were the most formidable of sages, surveying the laws of all creation from within. Aurena ordinarily regarded their achievements, in her heart, as mere waypoints anyone could reach through finite, mechanical procedures. Had she been born in their same era, she could readily have…. Yet on the other hand, Aurena, with the Q&A before her, set aside—for the first time in a very long while—any inclination to lock horns with anyone. It was not a question of whether she could intellectually overwhelm the sages before her, one by one. At any rate, to win the universally valid, irrefutable recognition of the many, she had to become a Full Moon, a sage of the Arcanum. And for that, she needed the unanimous, dissent-free assent of the panelists. "On the Dynamical Properties of Dreams—" One of the sages recited the title of the work. He seemed to have finally resolved to attempt something. "—here you have named the fundamental component, or force, that represents the dynamical properties of dreams 'Dissolution Force.' As a researcher, the point I would raise is—" Awaiting the rest, Aurena steadied her breath. "—why did you not name it the 'Aurena Force'? Such a pity." The wind went out of her. The other panelists, and even Aurena, ended up snickering. The remark was so absurd that they could not bring themselves to refuse the convivial impulse. But they could not go on lightening the mood like that forever. If one could come to grasp and apply Dissolution Force correctly, the Arcanum Society might seize power beyond that of a value-neutral, respected academic institution.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main1_Content_1:
"Throughout, it is conspicuous that you yourself designed, fabricated, and devised the new experimental apparatus, measuring instruments, and analytical techniques you adopted."
The sharp senses peculiar to the Anguillian bristled. It began now.
"This raises the concern that, lacking an understanding of the highly reproducible experimental protocols current in the established Society, you may have selectively cherry-picked—conveniently, and somewhat arbitrarily—the latitude of interpretation leading from process to analysis to results."
Aurena drew herself upright. It was a fairly sharp critique, but one she had anticipated to a degree. Though she had shown exceptional talent in mastering scholarship from a young age, she had been altogether hopeless in the relations between people; thus she had, all this while, disregarded every convention and custom of the Society wholesale, proving herself solely through results. So she had had no choice but to brace, to a degree, for fierce backlash.
"I have paid sufficient attention to securing the reliability of the novel apparatus, techniques, and methodology itself, which are not integrated with the established experimental protocols,"
she said.
"The capacity to take an approximation of the continuous object that is the Power of Dreams and to discretize and quantify it was indispensable, yet none of the existing equipment could meet the required performance; hence the method was adopted out of necessity. All instruments were calibrated to yield consistent values when used at room temperature and pressure, or in an equivalent average reaction environment, before being incorporated into the experimental design. The raw, unprocessed preliminary measurements obtained during calibration were also appended in full, reinforcing the formal legitimacy of the process."
"Why was a safety classification—adverse reactions and the like—omitted from the principal outcome-variable types in the experimental design?"
The second critique. As it took issue with the safety of the experimental participants, it carried more bite than the preceding remark.
"I was given to understand it was included in the initial form."
"The experiment adopted by this work is not a clinical study, and it contains no element that would warrant such a classification. That is precisely why, in sampling, an outline was approved that greatly compressed the requisite experiments through a Latin-square design in place of a between-participants design."
Aurena said.

"The safety item in the initial form was entered in the course of applying the common template verbatim. The experimental participants serve to contrast valid procedures for exerting Dissolution Force against invalid ones, and in that process it was concluded that the evidence is scant that Dissolution Force exerts any long-term effect upon a participant's body or system of cognition."
After that, the criticisms continued one after another. The gap between the theory developed in the work and the values derived and corrected through it; whether the trends among the observed values were somewhat too inconsistent to apply statistical significance mechanically; whether the experimental elements had been combined without mutual contradiction… But what worried Aurena most lay elsewhere. It was the statistical noise that, while conducting transformation experiments on diverse objects through diverse participants, could never be eliminated no matter what she did—and yet unmistakably existed. Even when she unified all other conditions and repeated the causal estimation, subtle deviations manifested differently from participant to participant.
More bewildering still was the fact that, despite endlessly repeating further iterations and approximations to nonlinear functions in order to rein in those values scattered so unwieldily, the deviations among participants were not resolved; rather, the observed values exhibiting those deviations converged, for each participant, upon multiple means that appeared to be a kind of intrinsic constant, distinct to each individual. To accept this directly would mean that the Power of Dreams reacts in wildly different ways according to the individual—that is, that the Power of Dreams is not a natural law but something like magic, operating differently for each participant. The more logical explanation, of course, appeared to be a systematic error at the level of measurement, and she had embedded that perspective in the work; yet she could not entirely set her mind at ease. At any rate, though it made her break out in a cold sweat, the Q&A concluded without incident, no decisive blow having landed. Aurena was asked to step out of the hall briefly and wait.
As she sat waiting, the soles of her shoes kept stamping the floor and dropping, over and over. Aurena knitted her brow irritably. It felt as though someone might come storming over to bellow at her on that account. Granted, it was a moment that warranted tension—but even accounting for that, she was severely shrunken in on herself. It was not failure she feared, but the aftermath of failure. For if the hidebound, exclusionary Arcanum Society refused to accept the very concept of the Power of Dreams, then no matter what innovative work she accomplished thereafter, she might be turned away at review again and again. And then, however much she flaunted her results, she might remain nothing but an unaffiliated scholar of the provinces, holding no stake whatsoever in the place where the continent's finest minds gathered—though that, in the end, amounted to no more than the difference between a snail and a snail with legs.
She had no idea how much time had passed.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main1_Content_2: * "We'll have to order new furniture and fittings for the spire, it seems." "Pardon?" At the words of a panelist who had opened the door and come out, Aurena was bewildered. She had been perched with barely her rear on the edge of her chair, and sprang up in a hurry; but at that utterly absurd remark, both body and mind froze halfway, in an awkward crouch. "Whatever do you mean…." "There has never been a Full Moon as young as you, after all. Were you simply to move in as is, much would be inconvenient." The panelist nodded and smiled. "Congratulations on becoming the youngest sage in the history of the Arcanum, Sage Aurena." She was overjoyed enough to leap. She thought hot tears might come gushing out. She thought she might bound giddily up and down and crack her golden horns against the ceiling. Yet when it actually became reality, she went blank. For a very brief moment her whole body felt buoyant, but that was all. After that, she simply went numb. If anything, the stray thoughts that now had no reason to be suppressed began to run rampant as never before. If that noise is not error—if there truly is no other way to interpret it—Aurena thought, reluctantly—if there is, for some reason, a fixed value like a constant intrinsic to each participant, by which the reaction pattern of Dissolution Force is differentiated, then must I regard it as actually interacting with each individual's body or system of cognition? Have I, then, conducted my research wrongly? It was the sort of problem hard to look away from, yet impossible to solve at once even if confronted. If a new, unorthodox force incompatible with the existing natural laws reacted differently from person to person on top of that, then research to confirm its safety would fall far short within a mere few days. It would become a matter demanding an ultra-long-term longitudinal study, tracking and observing numerous participants over months, even years. "Well, now that I've become a sage, at least I've bought myself that much time…." "What did you say?" Aurena waved her hand and shook her head as if it were nothing. The habit of talking to herself, formed in the course of research, would slip out abruptly now and then. Suddenly fatigue washed over her, and she even yawned. Her eyes were heavy. Her limbs hung slack. Ever since she had begun researching Dissolution Force, growing weary had become more frequent. There was nothing strange about it. It had been a difficult task, after all. I can simply research it further now, can't I? she thought. The dream world was not going to suddenly vanish somewhere, anyway, nor was there any chance of a dangerous turn of events in which rifts suddenly opened here and there and the scattered Dissolution Force came to be clumsily exploited. She stroked her golden horns proudly. They were not merely vainglorious ornaments, but, in themselves, the greatest proof of her achievement. She had yet to elucidate the principle, and they were closer to a byproduct generated by chance in the midst of an experiment; but that gold had unmistakably been "transmuted" through Dissolution Force, and, not stopping there, it maintained a state of being grafted on, as though it were Aurena's own body. "Once I keep researching and sweep away the noise completely—and now that I've even become a sage—it'll be smooth sailing." The soliloquy, hushed only just enough not to reach the panelist, leaked out again in a mutter. "That insufferable Aurena—they'll have no choice but to admit how far she surpasses them. And then everything will be complete!" Entering the hall with a snort, Aurena—busy as she was—took careful note of the silver brooch awarded only to the sages of the Arcanum. The official conferral ceremony was still far off, yet merely gazing at the chests of the panelists who wore it loosened her mouth into a foolish grin. That iridescent hue filled the whole room with radiance. Marveling quietly within, Aurena bowed her head to the panelists who had accepted her. "Thank you." However spirited and arrogant she might be, in that single phrase alone there was not the slightest falsehood.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main1_Short: She has stretched the laws of nature wide enough to admit a power no one else could name — yet a noise she cannot subtract from the data keeps whispering. What if she measured everything perfectly and understood nothing at all?
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main2_Content_0: The coffeehouse of the Arcanum Society was a rather unfamiliar concept to the rest of the continent's nations and peoples. Tourists who had given the Society only the most superficial glance commonly took the place for somewhere that sold beverages with a stimulant effect, and passed it by; but in truth it was, after the Society's Seven Spires and the Ether Library, the place where the most fervent scholarly debates—and, through them, collective action toward truth—were organized and carried out. People who ordered a drink and took a table would naturally pair off in twos and threes with those of like mind, or unlike, and carry on heated conversation. There were also matters as simple as forging acquaintance or lightly exchanging commercial information; but more than that, it was the collision of view against view that flourished. Ethics, philosophy, natural science, mathematics, chemistry… A volume of scholarly discourse that would make any printing house wag its tongue would, through mere talk—the play of lips and tongue—form an unprecedented new orthodoxy, while at other times an entire school of thought would be branded unfit and devalued. Someone had once argued that if one gathered every sound to be heard at the center of the coffeehouse at midday, there would surely be, within it, some combination that could not be rendered as a string of characters; and nearly all members of the Society held it to be a true proposition. At the very center of such a coffeehouse, Aurena was clutching a head that throbbed as though about to burst, letting out a groan. "So sleepy… why am I so sleepy?" Talking to herself had been quite helpful when she was lost in contemplation in her laboratory. It served not merely as grumbling, but as the finest means of stepping back from herself and grasping the situation—what she was doing, why, whether there was anything amiss in the hypothesis she had set, whether the experiment was properly holding together. But what spilled out unsuppressed even in a place like this, she wished to stem as far as possible. Aurena sniffed the pitch-black beverage that had spilled onto the saucer. The capillaries inside her nose dilated, and for some reason her salivary glands, her elbows, even the small of her back throbbed and surged—it was unmistakably a concentrated extract. Though she had gripped that contents, viscous as bitumen, by the body of the cup rather than the handle, and had tossed it down her throat in repeated, hurling gulps, why did the drowsiness still not lift? "It's my body that's the problem." She spread her hand and wrapped it around the side of the glass. "That can't be it. It's the shop that's the problem." She unconsciously put strength into the hand gripping the glass, but, naturally, nothing happened. "They've lowered the concentration. They have, truly." This clammy, foggy mood—as though the mist in her head were seeping out to cast its noise over every organ and tissue within her body—was, little by little, becoming familiar. To dispel it refreshingly required a larger motion. A movement of a scale impossible for Aurena's natural body alone was indispensable. She gave a slight grin, thinking of the golden horn ornament atop her head. There was a time I thought even this was enormous. Transmuting gold and grafting it on like a body part, then using it, had now become familiar. Too familiar. It was a thing she had become able to do precisely for that reason. The inside of her wrist itched. And so Aurena made to do something. For an act that was, to her, as natural as a stretch, she made to summon forth the ponderous mass of gold she had transmuted with Dissolution Force. Then she stopped. However little she cared for the eyes of others, she had no confidence she could withstand the storm that would break if she actually pulled "that" out at the center of a coffeehouse in broad daylight. "I'm so sorry!" Ah—into the ear of Aurena, who was bent over with her cheek laid against the table, behaving for all the world like a snake climbing a tree, came at last the voice she had been waiting for. Together with a slightly ragged breath, and the sound of feet striking the floor and dropping in rapid succession. Hmm. Mobilizing a sense of smell far keener than a human's, Aurena traced the traces of the past wafting off him. The young apprentice who hastily yanked out a chair and sat there gave off almost no scent of sweat. So he only pretended to hurry, she thought cynically. "I'm a little late—I truly apologize." "Yes, well…." Her tongue had stiffened, and the words would not come out smoothly. This was all the fault of her head, foggy as mist, and her limbs and her belly. Should she, unwillingly, have gotten a bit of sleep? Meanwhile, Aurena looked at the thick books the apprentice had tucked under his arm, untouched by any hand. The leather-bound volumes contained, jumbled together, all manner of radical theories—beginning with the theory of biological transition and including "The Worm of Reductionism." Those theories, which had failed to ripen into a single coherent body of scholarship and remained in the solipsistic state of mere eggshells holding a few intuitive relational pairs, had taken their place upon the comfortable table as though it were a nest that could shelter them from the upheavals of scientific methodology—Aurena thought, all the more, that she really ought to have forced herself to sleep first. At the same time, she could not help but scoff at the truly bizarre tendency that emerged among the young apprentices who sought her out for a private audience. The belief they tacitly shared could be explained in no other way than that someone at the Arcanum had lectured them: "If you want to get into Aurena's good graces, just pretend to be an ardent devotee of the alternative scientific theories that linger at the Society's periphery." When Aurena herself neither knew much about those theories, nor counted them among her specialties, nor had ever publicly professed support for them!
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main2_Content_1: "How obvious." "Sorry?" Aurena, still half-collapsed onto the desk, merely flailed her hand to signal that the words were not directed at him. A few feathers fluttered loose—feathers that had grown ever thinner and shallower-rooted ever since she had begun taking her meals out of sync with the cycle of day and night. "Because somehow, when it comes to that 'Aurena,' she's supposed to be a devotee who swoons over theories that look unconventional and radical." He wants somehow to get into the good graces of a sage who has gone so far as to name and research the Power of Dreams, but, knowing nothing of Dissolution Force, he therefore probes at this and that. How transparent it is, the way he approaches dropping whatever subject he can best pretend to know about—and surely they themselves are not unaware of it. "It's hot, isn't it? I feel it too." The apprentice, having taken Aurena's sigh entirely the wrong way—or having wished to believe so—struck up the conversation amiably. It was somehow mortifying to see right through the way he busied himself matching her rhythm. At any rate, the wish itself to study under a promising researcher could hardly be faulted, and even if it was pretense, the very effort to form common ground with the other party ought to be commended. Whether the motive was purely scholarly ardor alone, one could not vouch. "Have you thought over the proposal?" Aurena asked, raising her body upright and setting her appearance to rights. Smoothing the hem of her garment that had rolled up wherever her hands had wandered, drawing the collar closed, sweeping down fur that had risen in odd directions… and in doing so, she felt anew what an unkempt, ragamuffin state she was in. Her face threatened to grow a little hot. "Yes." The apprentice, oblivious to such complicated feelings of Aurena's, opened his mouth with a resolute expression. "I really want to work with you. No—not 'try' to work; I want to work in your laboratory, Sage!" "Yes, well…." Her back was stiff and sore. Aurena fitted the hollow of her back against the chair's backrest and, putting her weight into it, arched her spine far backward. While she was at it, she wanted to bring her arms up over her head, grip her elbows, and loosen her shoulders, but… she promptly gave it up and bent forward again. Then she quickly tidied the sleeves that had rolled up to bare her underarms. Was I too unguarded? she thought. Judging by how the apprentice's gaze wavered like a small boat caught in a squall on the open sea, it seemed so. If such small incidents could, as a result, draw in more assistants, there was nothing to lose. The assistants themselves might suppose they were useful only for simple repetitive tasks or strenuous menial labor; but, believe it or not, they could play a far greater role in Aurena's research. Whether they themselves wished it or not. "The fixed salary and the performance pay are all Society standard. Any separate operating funds you need, you apply for at headquarters, not at my laboratory." "Yes." Aurena turned her gaze away from the apprentice, who, if told to repeat what he had just heard, would be struck dumb. Following his gaze, fixed on one spot as though it were hearing her words in place of his ears, she found that the fur of her body had bristled up disheveled again and was basking in the sun in odd directions. She tidied it in a hurry while continuing to speak. "There's no opening in my laboratory at the moment, so for the time being you'll be set up temporarily in another sage's annex. Is that all ri—" "Yes, that's fine!" A brisk reply. After that came the usual formalities. Basic guidance on precautions, the exchange of necessary personnel-related or material matters… Aurena gazed steadily at the apprentice as he diligently read what was to be read and wrote what was to be written on the documents handed to him.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main2_Content_2: Reeled right in, she thought. As a starting line, it was not bad. It was the optimal reaction environment for issuing instructions in some gray zone—directions not overtly dangerous or unlawful, but that might look that way, or might not. And how could scholarly research, especially research dealing with so high-dimensional an object as the Power of Dreams, ever be cut by the two-toned black-and-white logic of what must clearly be done and what must absolutely not? Aurena had already finished, in her head, several experimental designs that she could "recommend"—ever so kindly—while leaving the final choice to the assistants. Ingesting orally an aqueous solution containing the essence of Dissolution Force, for instance, or contacting a transmuted substance whose properties had not yet been fully clarified and checking the reaction equation in that state…. Valid observations had to be obtained in as many situations and as many ways as possible. Especially when it came to the application and interpretation of Dissolution Force, a force of a world other than reality, every kind of interaction was indispensable. "So have confidence in yourself." Aurena whispered softly—however frantic she might be, she could manage that much discernment. She had to! "You aren't a green, blunder-prone assistant who only blusters with his mouth about working hard. You are the finest…." At that moment the apprentice, having finished signing, held out the paper. After that came, once more, the messy formalities of one kind and another. A moment of shaking hands and exchanging words like "I'll see you tomorrow," "Yes, it's your first day, so just bring yourself," passed, and Aurena was again sitting alone at the table. Watching the apprentice's back receding into the distance, she furrowed her brow. Not on account of any emotion, but purely from fatigue. "This is maddening, truly." Now the sense of helplessness filling her head and body and belly felt no longer like mist, but like a stream of water poured outright from a basin. A pressure pressing in, plump and heavy, from inside the tough, supple sacks and pouches and bundles—or, conversely, the negative pressure of a void felt when something is absent. The feeling that somewhere in her body was empty and kept leaking away held Aurena and would not let her go. She thrust out her arm before she knew it. She made to perform the habit she had barely suppressed before the apprentice arrived—the large movement that could dispel this feeling refreshingly. Amid the teeming throng of the Arcanum coffeehouse, something like an alien shadow shimmered for a moment. A form shaped like a gilded folding fan, yet far too immense to be held meekly in anyone's hand, undulated, made to encroach upon part of the material world… and hastily vanished. "…Not here." Aurena said. She felt irritation and fatigue piled layer upon layer, painfully tugging at her two eyelids, both shoulders, her limbs. The cup she had just gripped and set down, the table, the chair, the railing of the coffeehouse and its plank-paneled floor… she wanted to claw and rip them all to shreds, to dig everything up into a chaotic ruin as though plucking lint from a garment. She wanted to snap them off bit by bit and strew the pieces about until head and tail were indistinguishable. As soon as she got home, then, she would summon a transmuted object and make a grand commotion of it—but she could not. Aurena clutched her face in both hands and breathed hot breath into them. She smelled a stale, sweetish odor, mingled with the stimulant beverage, like that of one who has worked herself to death for days on end. "…When I get back, first thing, I'll sleep." For she was far too tired to do otherwise.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main2_Short: A weariness no draught can lift, and a gesture she barely keeps from loosing in a crowded room. When the subject of the experiment turns out to be a person, who decides the moment it begins?
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main2_Title: Theoretical Background - Research Purpose and Scope
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main3_Content_0: "Sage Aurena?" A light knocking on the door followed. "Sage Aurena?" A somewhat strained tone. At the same time, the hapless door—which had no idea what wrong it had committed—now began, instead of being knocked upon, to be struck. The sound grew so utterly different and savage that it was hard to believe it was the same kind of event—the impact of elastic deformation transmitted through a medium—caused by the same two substances, someone's hand and a wooden door panel. "Either she won't come out, or she's bolted…." "Move." Voices other than the one that had first knocked passed back and forth. Before long, a "whoosh" of ponderous wind blew. The door, struck full by a mace, had its hinge portion shattered clean off and torn away. The door swung open wide like a blossoming flower bud, and—as if even that were not enough—feet shod with thick rubber soles came kicking it open with bangs and bursting in. "Aurena! We are the Inspectorate, under the Ethics Committee!" Spirited as their entry was, the scene that unfolded before their eyes was thoroughly desolate. Not in the sense that there were many terrible things, but that it had been emptied bare. The various fittings, including the experimental apparatus, the records Aurena herself had written down… everything that could be carried off had been carried off. Even the contents of the flasks, discolored reddish or yellowish, had all been emptied out, then rinsed clean with fresh water and dried with cloth—a sight chilling enough to raise gooseflesh. It surely meant she intended both to block any pursuit so thoroughly, and at the same time to leave no room for anyone to imitate her research. And yet it was precisely that inhuman research, which no one wished to undertake, that had fallen out of the Society's favor in the first place. "Bolted clean away." "Nothing to see here." The Inspectorate members sighed and scattered throughout the laboratory. Befitting the home base—no, the lair—of one renowned for managing her experimental environment with obsessive compulsion, things were well-ordered and easy to find, but there was no substance to them. Whether the owner might return if they waited a while, whether she might be hiding somewhere and trembling… they were all too seasoned in this sort of work to entertain such hopes. The traces of one who had fled with no intention of ever returning, and those of one who had not, could be told apart at a glance. All the more so in a case as serious as Aurena's. "That she deceived an unspecified many—apprentices, scholarship students, and tourists among them—and included them in her experimental design." One Inspectorate member, rifling through the laboratory, broached the matter. "That she failed to fulfill her duty to disclose, despite the possibility of inflicting degeneration of the body and the system of cognition, or effects of comparable gravity." "That she did not obtain written consent from the experimental participants in accordance with the Society's standard form." The most important point, however, had not yet been spoken. "That, in the end, casualties resulted." The Inspectorate members fell silent each of their own accord, not on any instruction. They observed a moment of mourning welling up from the heart. That silence was broken abruptly—yet in the direction everyone had hoped for. "There's something here!" At the first breakthrough discovered, the Inspectorate members rushed over, delighted. Amid all manner of household items mostly hexahedral in form—their twelve edges all meeting at perfect ninety-degree right angles, or running parallel as two lines that would never meet—there was one object that had rolled in beneath the leg of something and, covered in dust, had succeeded in evading Aurena's surveillance net. "A standard Resonant Quartz." said the member who had picked it up. There was no reason to drag things out any longer. 「Shall I give it a try? Does this thing even work?」 When he wiped off the dust and repeated the prescribed operation, the voice of the user recorded in the quartz—in this case, Aurena's own voice—slowly began to issue forth. Everyone listened closely. 「Did I get swindled? Tsk.」 And then came sounds of bustling about, gripping the object and setting it down and so forth, as though she were doing something. 「This is an official Society vendor… well, of course—just because they put on a mortarboard and a robe, where do a snail's brains go? It'd be stranger if I didn't get swindled, heh heh.」 The Inspectorate members listening clenched their fists. To call the Society's other esteemed members snails, on the grounds that their thinking was sluggish, was a long-standing habit of Aurena's. They had heard she had restrained herself somewhat during her Half Moon days, but that after seizing a lifetime sage's seat at the youngest age in history, she had ceaselessly disparaged everyone around her—like a sun-stricken horse foaming at the mouth—and this, too, they knew. 「Oh! It works. So it was recording….」 "Sounds like a recording from when she first bought it." "Nothing much here. Skip ahead." The member holding the quartz complied. A rapidly compressed and distorted speech droned on like that for a while. Then, midway, the hand operating it suddenly halted. The other Inspectorate members listening swallowed their breath, blinked, or needlessly shifted the foot they stood on. It was on account of some uncanny sound. SKREEEEEK It was not that sort of sound. In truth, it could have been any sound at all. Just as a bird does not cry out in the neat, complete graphic letters "tweet, tweet," the sound was simply some unpleasant noise. The listeners knit their brows, but only for a moment; the words continued to issue forth. 「—am not.」 It was Aurena. A tone as though she had resolved upon something—or was huffing, unable to master her indignation. 「They're merely test subjects who have trouble saying that they are test subjects. Our walking snails, steeped in inertia as they are, would call this 'justification,' but….」 The rustle of garments and the creak of wooden furniture came next. Aurena seemed to have shrugged her shoulders while seated in a chair, marveling at how flawless her own thinking was. 「I have nothing whatsoever to justify, do I?」 SKREEEEEK The strange sound returned.
ui.TravelerStory_Aurena_Main3_Content_1: 「It's clear enough if you think about how the Arcanum came to be… there were those who discerned that their intellectual capacity was distinctly prominent, superior, excellent—at any rate, that they were different to a degree they could not be understood. And so they founded the Society, abolished some of the rules of the outside world, and designed their own peculiar systems of verification and rules according to their own needs.」 Aurena paused briefly, but not for long. It was surely a view she had been resolving upon all along. 「So why, then, must I—who am plainly far more superior even than the Arcanum, and different to a degree I cannot be understood—not pursue my own peculiar system of verification and rules?」 The Inspectorate members shuddered. The voice the quartz had preserved was so vivid. Vivid enough that one could tell what dwelt within it was no hasty hostility or callow petulance. The user—Aurena—was purely curious. If anything, she was exasperated with the other sages who failed to understand. 「While taking it as a matter of course, of course, that the intellectual capacity of the Society's members and the system of cognition that executes it cannot be understood by the continent's other nations and peoples, who fall short of even that—why can't I fathom why these walking snails believe they must not merely understand my system of cognition but be actively trained to it—ah, of course, these fellows have every right of resistance they can muster.」 The sound of clapping followed, and then, before long, that strange noise again. SKREEEEEK 「A rat biting the experimenter's finger as it wraps around its spine is not a matter of right and wrong, but an innate right of self-preservation. Likewise, the Society's walking snails may, in the end, resist if my own peculiar rules and system pose a threat to them… but. If that is so, then they are not punishing me. They have no such authority.」 Aurena's laughter swirled bleakly through the laboratory. 「So what can they do? Push it through by sheer numbers, and by appeals to principle.」 She went on, clicking her tongue. 「First subdue me, an individual, with the physical force of the collective that is the Society; then condemn me by tacking on every principle that can possibly be tacked on. The trouble is that they won't think of the process that way.
